I have strong, multiple, unambiguous confirmations. Let me finalize my answer with the clearest, most explicit example.

## Answer

**Yes.** Caddy has raised its minimum Go version multiple times specifically because of upgrades to `quic-go` — the third-party library that implements Caddy's HTTP/3 support (`github.com/quic-go/quic-go`, imported directly in `modules/caddyhttp/server.go` and `listeners.go` for the HTTP/3 listener/transport).

### Primary supporting commit

**`8cb1bb4af30b880f981b1ae6fdb13e5944bfaefe`** — *"go.mod: Upgrade quic-go to v0.33.0 (Go 1.19 min)"* (Matthew Holt, 2023-02-24)

The commit message itself states the causal link in its title: the quic-go upgrade to v0.33.0 required Go 1.19 as the minimum. The diff shows:

`go.mod`:
```diff
-	github.com/quic-go/quic-go v0.32.0
+	github.com/quic-go/quic-go v0.33.0
```
(plus corresponding `qtls-go1-19`/`qtls-go1-20` bumps used by quic-go's TLS stack)

`README.md`:
```diff
 Requirements:

-- [Go 1.18 or newer](https://golang.org/dl/)
+- [Go 1.19 or newer](https://golang.org/dl/)
```

There is no other unrelated change in this commit — it's exclusively a quic-go dependency bump paired with the Go minimum-version bump, making the causality explicit.

### Corroborating commits (same pattern repeated later)

- **`f45a6de20dd19e82e58c85b37e03957b2203b544`** — *"go.mod: Update quic-go to v0.37.0, bump to Go 1.20 minimum (#5644)"* (Marten Seemann, 2023-07-22). Title again directly ties the quic-go update to the Go minimum bump; diff moves `go.mod` from `go 1.19` to `go 1.20` alongside `quic-go v0.36.2` → `v0.37.0`.

- **`697cc593a17fcb39087161b058fc1dba8b767060`** — *"chore: Update quic-go to v0.41.0, bump Go minimum to 1.21 (#6043)"* (Marten Seemann, 2024-01-25). Same pattern: `quic-go v0.40.1` → `v0.41.0`, `go.mod` `go 1.20` → `go 1.21`, README requirement bumped to "Go 1.21 or newer."

All three commits were authored either by Matthew Holt (Caddy's creator) or Marten Seemann (quic-go's maintainer), and each commit's title explicitly states the quic-go/HTTP-3-library version bump as the reason for the Go minimum version increase — this wasn't incidental; it happened repeatedly as a recurring pattern whenever quic-go itself raised its own Go version requirement.
